name: base16
short_description: A human-readable, compact binary encoding using a character set designed to minimize human transcription errors.
long_description: Base16 is a hexadecimal-like encoding system that uses a carefully chosen alphabet (A, B, C, D, E, G, H, K, P, R, S, T, W, X, Y, Z) instead of the standard 0-9a-f characters. It is designed to minimize user frustration and transcription errors when dealing with high-entropy data such as voucher codes, confirmation codes, and verification tokens. The project includes error-correction capability that automatically maps similar-looking invalid characters to the correct base16 characters based on 1983 research on human transcription errors. It provides both a Python library API and a command-line interface for encoding, decoding, and generating random base16 strings.

modules.description: Core encoding and decoding logic with character mapping tables and fuzzy matching for similar-looking characters.
Package initialization that exports public API functions (encode, decode, random, encode_hex, decode_hex).
Command-line interface implementation with argument parsing for encode, decode, and random operations.
Test suite covering encoding, decoding with strict/fuzzy modes, hex operations, random generation, and performance benchmarks.
